clue.text: Wrong name for anarchic modernism that hasn't died

indicators.note: anarchic means without order or rule, so these letters are thrown into a new sequence
D is the standard abbreviation for died, and saying something hasn't it means that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A critic complains that 'anarchic' is the wrong label for a modernist movement that is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D (died) from MODERNISM to leave MOERNISM, then rearrange those eight letters to get MISNOMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is an inaccurate or unsuitable label given to a person or thing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Something for breakfast is made of rice? Really!

indicators.note: what something is made of is its material, so the letters are drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to learn that a breakfast food is made from rice.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation breaks the surface in two, but the hidden run ignores it: riCE REALly.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast cereals such as cornflakes or puffed rice are typical morning foods eaten with milk.

clue.text: Sailor gets posted away

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a letter that is posted is sent

explanation.surface: A sailor receives orders that send him off to a distant station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted away' reads as one phrase about a posting, but 'away' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away is not present at a place, which is what being absent means.

clue.text: Whirlwind caused by a Musk company having a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and changing it swaps that letter for another

parts.note: Elon Musk bought the social network Twitter in 2022

explanation.surface: A storm of controversy is blamed on one of Elon Musk's businesses changing its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of TWITTER, its fourth T, is changed to S. 'Change of heart' usually means a change of mind; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an informal American term for a tornado, a violently rotating column of wind.

clue.text: Stupendous borders edged with flowers and yet more flowers

indicators.note: to be edged with something is to have it all round you, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: blooms are flowers

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, the first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A garden boasts magnificent borders fringed with flowers and then even more flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' appears twice: the first is wordplay giving BLOOMS, the second, with 'yet more', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossoms are the flowers of a plant, especially fruit trees, so they are further flowers after the blooms.

clue.text: Ten made to run around without information, forgetting disorder

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece stands round another
running around is moving about without a fixed course, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: Ten people are sent running about without being told anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense of outside. 'Forgetting disorder' is a single noun phrase, a disorder of forgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a medical condition marked by progressive memory loss and declining mental ability.

clue.text: Position sculpture, replacing the pedestal

indicators.note: a pedestal is the base an object stands on, and in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, which is swapped

parts.note: a statue is a sculpture

explanation.surface: Instructions for installing a sculpture by swapping out its plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the last letter sits at the bottom like a pedestal: the E of STATUE is replaced with S.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank in society, which is a common sense of position.

clue.text: Explosive news items led mob into acts of torture

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: four words, fifteen letters, taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Inflammatory news reports whip a crowd up into committing atrocities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive news' is a natural phrase, but 'Explosive' is the signal and every letter of the next four words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Disembowelment, cutting out the entrails, was a historical method of execution and torture.

clue.text: It may signal a cold snap beginning to affect the audience's leg joints

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its opening letter

indicators.note: what an audience gets is what it hears, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: the joints in the middle of the leg, said out loud

explanation.surface: A sudden cold spell is said to bring on aching knees in the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cold snap' is a weather phrase, but 'a cold' belongs to the definition and 'snap' is wordplay. KNEES and NEEZE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneezing is one of the first symptoms of a common cold, so it can warn that an infection is starting.

clue.text: American quietly infiltrates splinter groups and has a sense of foreboding

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: sects are breakaway groups
US for American
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An American agent secretly works his way into breakaway factions and senses trouble ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from the musical direction piano. 'Has a sense of foreboding' is a verb phrase, matching the third-person verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to have an uneasy feeling that something bad is true or about to happen.

clue.text: Something tasty is revealed in some letters

indicators.note: something revealed in a place was there all along, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A secret or a delicious detail comes to light in a bundle of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run is sOME LETTErs; 'some' doubles as part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a savoury dish of beaten eggs fried in a pan, a tasty thing to eat.

clue.text: Insensitive to be unruly around us

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other
unruly means disorderly and out of control, so these letters do not keep their order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that it is tactless to behave badly in their company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be' looks like the link between definition and wordplay, but its four letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An obtuse person is slow to understand or notice feelings, so dull and tactless in manner.

clue.text: Fifth day of the week comes to a close with a sitcom

parts.note: Friday, counting the week from Monday, abbreviated
something that comes to a close ends

explanation.surface: The working week winds down on a Friday with a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: FRI is the standard calendar abbreviation for Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends is the long-running American television comedy about six young New Yorkers, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Throw out curate or penpusher in Brussels?

indicators.note: throwing things out tosses them about, so these letters land in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A choice is offered: expel a clergyman or a Belgian civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' reads as expel, but it signals rearranging, and 'or' is part of the fodder, not a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an official of the European Union bureaucracy, headquartered in Brussels; a penpusher is a clerk.

clue.text: Admit car must be redesigned to be striking

indicators.note: something redesigned is reworked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A designer concedes that a car needs a makeover to look eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is fodder together with 'car'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is vivid and impressive enough to catch the eye, as is something striking.

clue.text: Fitting handle takes expert

parts.note: to handle a tool is to use it
an expert is able, skilled

explanation.surface: Fitting a door handle is a job that needs a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like a verb about installation; it is an adjective meaning suitable. The usual spelling is usable, and useable is an accepted variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting is suitable for its purpose, and so fit to be put to service.

clue.text: Lion injured poor mule on the floor, maybe?

definitions.note: the definition describes where the answer is found rather than naming it

indicators.note: an injured body is knocked out of shape, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: something in poor condition is in a bad way, so these letters are jumbled too

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An injured lion and a sickly mule lie stricken on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Each animal is rearranged separately, each with its own signal, and the two results are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a durable sheet covering laid in kitchens and hallways, so it is a thing found underfoot.

clue.text: Provided food and showed concern about evacuated tribe

indicators.note: about can mean round, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: to care is to show concern

indicators.note: an evacuated building has been emptied, so the word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: the word with its middle emptied out

explanation.surface: Aid workers fed and looked after a displaced tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated tribe' suggests refugees, but evacuated means emptied: the word loses everything but its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply meals for an event or group, so catered is past tense of that.

clue.text: Log off and switch over broadcast of Ms Swanson, perhaps

indicators.note: something off is not right, out of its proper state, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: switching something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it

explanation.surface: Someone logs off their computer and changes channel to catch a programme about the film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log off' looks like signing out of a computer; 'off' rearranges LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood silent-film star, so she is one example of a person with the name.

clue.text: Allow entertaining rogue to serve up shellfish

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in your home, so one piece takes another in

parts.note: to allow is to let
an imp is a mischievous little rascal

explanation.surface: A host lets a charming scoundrel dish up seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' reads as an adjective meaning amusing, but it is a verb: LET entertains IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a sea creature with a conical shell that clings to rocks, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: Tragic heroine skedaddled after protester

indicators.note: after sets the order, sending the piece named before it to the second position

parts.note: an anti is someone who opposes something
someone who has skedaddled has gone

explanation.surface: The leading lady of a tragedy ran off after encountering a protester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order: the word for skedaddled comes after the word for protester.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is the title character of Sophocles' Greek tragedy, who defies the king to bury her brother.

clue.text: Do they have a go at hearing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who make an attempt
second meaning: those who judge a case in court

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one question about having a go at hearing; split it, and a hearing is a court session where cases are tried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tries hard makes attempts, and a judge or juror who tries a case decides it at a court hearing.

clue.text: Health food found on the golf course?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the smooth putting areas around each hole

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke of finding vegetables on a golf course; the word has a separate golfing meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy vegetables like cabbage and spinach are nutritious, and a golf course has a closely mown putting surface at every hole.

clue.text: I came back and consumed waste

indicators.note: going back means going the opposite way, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: taken as written
food consumed is eaten

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they returned and polished off the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' looks like a noun for rubbish, but it is a verb, as in waste away.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to become or make abnormally thin, the sense of the verb in wasting away.

clue.text: Models of perfection unsettled ladies …

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed from its place, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Images of perfect beauty leave women feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this surface to the next clue but has no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard or example of excellence that people aim at, a model of perfection.

clue.text: … who, for example, ate liver casserole for sister eating nothing

indicators.note: a casserole is a stew of mixed ingredients, so these letters are stirred together

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a nun is a sister in a religious order
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, someone cooked liver for a sister who was fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casserole' reads as the dish being eaten, but it signals the rearrangement; 'eating nothing' puts O inside NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Who introduces clauses that refer back to a noun, as in 'the man who came', making it a grammatical relative pronoun.
